title: Exposure psychology, bias-aware slice selection — lab journal (wip)
content:
Purpose / quick pitch:
This is a working journal for designing slice selection and stakeholder cadence that explicitly accounts for human cognitive biases during phased exposure. The goal: reduce false positives in human signal, avoid overreacting to noisy short-term spikes, and speed up safe rollouts for LLM-powered features.

High-level problem framing (notes to self):
- Engineers and PMs often interpret short blips in accuracy/latency as system regressions and roll back prematurely.
- Ops teams prefer conservative thresholds; product wants faster exposure.
- We need a shared protocol that encodes both statistical smoothing and human signal conditioning.

Key behavioral biases to account for:
- Availability bias: Recent incidents weigh too heavily in decision calls.
- Anchoring: Early metrics (first 1–2 hours) anchor downstream perceptions.
- Confirmation bias: Reviewers focus on examples that confirm expected regressions.
- Negativity bias: Bad outputs are more memorable than slightly better latency or cost.

Practical patterns / heuristics to mitigate biases:
1) Warm-bucket anchoring: always show a rolling baseline (7d avg + 95th pct band) alongside live charts so reviewers have context.
2) Pulse checks window: first 60 minutes labeled as "initialization" (analytics smoothing applied) — no stakeholder escalations unless severity > P0 rules.
3) Snapshot sampling: surface 50 random examples, 10 edge-cases, and 5 customer-reported examples for human review panels. Mix positives and negatives.
4) Decision latency rule: require 2 independent signals across orthogonal metrics (quality + downstream conversion OR latency + error rate) sustained for a min duration before rollback vote.

Slice-selection approach (bias-aware):
- Micro-slices: narrow, interpretable cohorts (e.g., onboarding flows, premium chat, low-connectivity sessions). Prioritize slices that are high user-impact and easy to validate.
- Synthetic stress slices: artificially increased load or adversarial prompts to surface regressions early in a quarantined bucket.
- Distribution drift slices: recent-traffic-only slice to detect sudden input shifts.
- Rare-event slices: low-volume but high-risk patterns (billing, personal-data-handling).

Guidelines for picking slices per feature launch:
- Must include at least one conversion-sensitive slice (e.g., checkout-text-generation) and one safety-sensitive slice.
- Limit to 4–6 slices for first-day monitoring to avoid analyst fatigue.
- Assign an owner for each slice (who will check examples and escalate).

Traffic partitioning schedule (example cadence):
- T0: 0% -> smoke tests internal (synth traffic only). Verify basic success criteria.
- T1 (1–4h): 0.5% user traffic to micro-slices + synthetic stress. Live baseline comparison, pulse-checks disabled for first 60m.
- T2 (24h): 2% to broader cohort, enable human sampling review twice per day.
- T3 (72h): 10% if no issues, enable automated quality regressors and longer term metrics.
- T4: progressive ramp to 50%+ using adaptive gating (cost/latency fallback triggers).

Decision criteria (quick checklist):
- Safety violation? (explicit P0 pattern) -> Immediate rollback.
- Quality drop > X% on slice AND drop sustained for Y windows -> escalate. (We need to quantify X/Y per feature; defaults: X=3 pts absolute on our ROUGE/QA-score proxy, Y=3 consecutive 10m windows after smoothing)
- Latency increase > 30% + user-visible errors -> hold and investigate.
- Cost per token increase > 2x expected -> notify finance + SRE; consider throttling.

Signal instrumentation notes:
- Report both raw and smoothed signals. Smoothing policy: EWMA with alpha tuned for volume; fallback to simple moving avg for low-volume slices.
- Include sample counts, p99/p95 latency, per-token cost, top-20 user examples flagged by anomaly detector.
- Add a human-review flag in analytics so manual triage events are recorded as annotations.

Human review workflow (ops-friendly):
- Triage board shows: slice name, sample set, auto-summary (concise classifier: hallucination / prompt-leak / harmful content / ok), one-click tag (false-positive, regress, needs-more-samples).
- Require at least 3 reviewers for any escalatory 'regress' tag during first 24h. Reviewers can be cross-functional: product / SRE / safety.
- Keep review sessions limited to 15m with a structured script to avoid anchoring: start with blind sampling, then show context.

Fallback and graceful degradation patterns:
- Soft fallback: route to cheaper/shorter model variant with transparent label if quality drops slightly.
- Hard fallback: route all traffic to previous model if P0 safety triggers.
- Feature toggles must support partial-response fallback (e.g., strip risky actions and show apology) for user-facing flows.

Communication & cadence (who hears what and when):
- Immediate: automated Slack alert to #prod-rollouts + SRE on P0s and hard fallbacks.
- Hourly: the active rollout channel gets a short pulse: "T1-2h: latency 1.2x, quality +0.6pt vs baseline; no safety flags."
- Daily: concise report to stakeholders with top-3 slices and action items.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantify default X/Y thresholds per product vertical (growth vs core-transactional flows).
- Define canonical "initialization" windows per model family (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder).
- Buy-in from legal/safety on synthetic stress slice definitions (customer-data handling).
- Integrate human-review annotations into rollout audit logs for postmortem.

Mini checklist for next sprint (owner: Priya):
- [ ] Prototype the triage board view (sample + auto-summary) — link to GH PR above.
- [ ] Run tabletop with PMs + SREs on a simulated 2% T2 bump using synthetic stress slices.
- [ ] Draft stakeholder comms templates (1h, 4h, 24h).
- [ ] Propose default EWMA smoothing alphas for high/med/low volume.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally behavioral-first — we will map thresholds to code after we validate stakeholder reactions in the tabletop. Expect a follow-up with concrete metric thresholds and an SRE-signed runbook.

Random examples (for UX copy tests):
- "During the first hour metrics will be noisy due to cache warm-up. Please rely on the 24h baseline for major decisions."
- "If human review tags a sample as 'regress' please add the sample id to the triage ticket to preserve context."

End of journal entry — next checkpoint: run demo on 2026-03-15 tabletop.
